findings.title: Post-enqueue submission failure duplicates settlement effects and permits callbacks after receipt
findings.scenario: S3 and S5: settlement submission, callback/source/waiter ordering
findings.summary: A non-shutdown RuntimeError can follow ThreadPoolExecutor queue publication; CheckedExecutor preserves that error and DownloadService responds by settling inline while the queued or already-running worker remains eligible. Transaction retirement has one winner but transaction_done has no entry latch, so both invocations execute object, transaction and outcome callbacks and source release attempts. Receipt ownership only guards the final stored outcome after those effects. A 77-state counterexample violates SingleSettlementEffects; a separate 94-state counterexample in MC_hunt_s3_after_receipt_bfs.out violates NoSettlementEffectsAfterReceipt. The provenance-checked existing local trace supports this mechanism under a controlled submit-failure injection, without establishing a natural production trigger or independent Phase 4 reproduction.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 3 and the callback/source/waiter-ordering portion of Scenario 5 (same post-enqueue settlement duplication mechanism)

findings.title: A pipelined EOF can publish COMPLETED progress after cancellation finalized FAILED
findings.scenario: S1: receiver truth versus terminal source progress
findings.summary: A supported Consumer pipeline admits its next request before consume fails and sends acquired-receiver cancellation. Cancellation commits final FAILED under the ref lock, then performs callbacks and FAILED progress outside that lock. An admitted EOF in this gap sees the already-final receiver, receives no serve nonce, and the terminal handler incorrectly selects COMPLETED progress from EOF even though confirmation is enabled. The first-terminal latch suppresses the later FAILED correction, as shown by a source-mapped 35-state TLC counterexample. The exact contradictory-progress schedule has not been independently reproduced at runtime, and neither a false successful strict receipt nor false trainer-send success is established.
findings.dedup_note: also covers code-review Scenario 1 (same final-status/progress split mechanism)

findings.title: Caller receiver declarations can diverge from complete-payload outcome semantics
findings.scenario: Scenario 2: Complete-payload receiver sets and caller fanout declarations
findings.summary: Scenario 2 asks whether transaction completion, success and quorum are interpreted against the receiver declaration actually supplied by the caller across every registered reference. The MC findings do not cover this mechanism: explicit identity mode is modeled as base semantics and no MC violation was emitted for aggregation itself. The brief preserves a caller-side regression hypothesis where multi-target Cell._fire_and_forget omits receiver metadata when encoding once, causing ViaDownloader to default to count 1 while non-pass-through broadcast paths provide count and identities. Confirmation should decide whether this underdeclared fanout can retire source lifetime or report outcomes inconsistently in a supported path.

findings.title: Receiver budget diagnostics and activity clocks remain review-only
findings.scenario: Scenario 4: Receiver budgets and transaction inactivity are different clocks
findings.summary: Scenario 4 separates per-receiver acquisition and idle budgets from transaction-wide inactivity, which is refreshed by any receiver. The MC run explored S4 budget behavior without emitting a violation, so no MC candidate carries this scenario as a concrete counterexample. The remaining code-review candidate is the diagnostic and semantics hypothesis that the warning for a receiver budget greater than or equal to the global inactivity timeout incorrectly says enforcement is disabled even though the sliding inactivity clock still allows receiver-budget enforcement. Confirmation should preserve the distinct transaction, receiver and progress clocks and decide whether the review-only diagnostic or any unmodeled schedule is actionable.

findings.title: Receipt retention, acquired-receiver visibility and source-lifetime documentation residuals
findings.scenario: Scenario 5: Source release, receipt retention, and waiter observations
findings.summary: Scenario 5 spans final receiver information, callback completion, source release attempts, receipt recording, waiter resolution, shutdown and caller observations. MC-1 covers the distinct post-enqueue duplicate-settlement part of this scenario, but it does not cover the separate review items at the receipt-retention, acquired-receiver-query and source-lifetime documentation sites. The brief calls out unswept expired receipts that can resolve new waiters while outcome query expires them, acquired_receivers() returning empty after retirement, and a stale CacheableObject comment about source release and produce overlap. Confirmation should evaluate those residual mechanisms separately from MC-1 because they cite different code sites and have no model-checking counterexample here.
